terms.comment: Classically one who travels about; Morgan–Owens adds religiōnis causā, after Egger, where the context does not make the purpose plain.

evidence: Vulg. Lc. 24.18: Tū sōlus peregrīnus es in Jerusalem
terms.comment: The medieval word for a pilgrim, whence English pilgrim; classically, and in the Vulgate, a foreigner or a visitor.

sources: Lewis & Short: peregrinator · Lewis & Short: peregrinus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. pilgrim.
